One of the key factors in Lisa's arc in VisionQuest is the deep dynamic she shares with Tommy. However, unlike other TV shows and films where a female character's whole purpose becomes only about serving the male character, the series really explores how Lisa is Tommy's whole world prior to him reconnecting with Vision, while letting her shine outside of their relationship.

When asked if that was something that she enjoyed portraying throughout the season, Morais explained how she cares for Tommy, and how she was able to use her own experience to guide him:

Lauren Morais: "It was so fun to develop that and see that in the script. You meet them both on the bus, and he's about to have a panic attack, and she talks him through it, and she talks through her own survival modes of it, and she got him into the scamming and the pickpocket life, and I thought that was a nice juxtaposition to maybe what we've seen before, but I think all in all, they just really look after each other, and I love that.

Like you said, it's not like Lisa's hanging on to him. It's more like we share a similar past of orphanhood and not belonging, so we're going to stick with each other and look after each other because there's this weird, random connection that instant that you can't really explain. But it's there, and I'm ready to go through this wild journey of finding out that your dad's like a robot. What Lisa thinks, she's still figuring it out, as you can see. But she accepts it because she accepts Tommy in any form he is."

The MCU did a variation of Lisa's Coat of Arms, but with a more grounded approach. While it's not fully Tiboro's Coat from the comics, Morais was excited to see the VisionQuest series honor it in its own way, as she shared how she learned that they were taking this direction with it.

Lauren Morais: "I saw it when I was reading the scripts, it was in one of the stages, like the directions, Lisa has this blazer and has fake arms, and she's pickpocketing. And I thought that was such a fun taste for the audience of Lisa, and also it made sense with her character of being a pickpocket and surviving on the streets.

I thought that was very, very clever, and also as an actor, it was so funny on set, having those arms and that blazer, going to shake people's hands. I gave some people a high five, and some people on the crew hadn't seen the script, so they were very confused when I suddenly had four arms. And I was like, "I'm in Marvel now, I have four arms. This is how it goes, guys!"

As Lisa and Tommy take off with Paladin in the end, Morais was asked if that was perhaps leading to the MCU's Young Masters, or perhaps a variation of the darker team from the comics, as the group is traditionally a group of villains. In terms of what the future has in store for Lisa, she is hoping to see more for her character after the finale:

Lauren Morais: That's up to the Marvel gods, but I think what I would personally love to explore is Lisa's villainy and the Young Masters and her relationship with Tommy going forward. I think that would be so exciting, and taking bits from the comics, and also seeing what she can do with the drone and the forearms and with DUM-E and U. That's what I would love to explore is her and her powers and what she's going to do with them. Is she gonna go for the superhero vibe or the villain vibe? I don't know, but I want to see that.

VisionQuest episode 8 sees the Maximoff brothers finally reunited, as Joe Locke's Billy returned and shared the screen with Ruardih Mollica's Tommy. When asked if there was a version of finale where Lisa and Wiccan got to interact more, Morais responded with the following:

Lauren Morais: I think those are conversations that, when I was thinking about that, is what Tommy and Lisa would have. When they go to the motel, and she's doing the drowning. To me, that was all encompassed in that moment. And as we build up to the finale, those [are] definitely things that Tommy and Lisa have considered. But also, as you can see, I think it was episode four, Tommy says about Vision being his dad, and she just kind of accepts it. She's kind. She trusts Tommy with her whole heart that I think as long as Tommy thinks what he's doing is right, and she'll go with him anywhere. She'll defend him, and if he's in trouble, she knows who to call.

ScreenRant: It seemed like everyone around them was just accusing him of being crazy. But she just kind of accepted it.

Lauren Morais: I think she's gone through so much herself, and she has so much innate trust in him. She's like, 'Yeah, of course, whatever. I'll be by your side because we have each other. We only have each other in this crazy world,' and I don't think she'll [ever] abandon [Tommy] because [they have] gone [a lot.] They've done the [pick-]pocketing, they've been living together in this crazy world without much family - [but] they have each other, I think she's an easygoing girl as well.

While the VisionQuest show is really the end of this trilogy, there could always be more spinoffs, as Bettany's drama was another offshoot. When sharing that the MCU has hopefully not seen the last of Lisa, Morais stressed how she had the best time:

Lauren Morais: "Oh, thank you! I mean, that would be so fun. I've had the best time, the absolute best time, and it's been so cool to see the fan reactions and the theories and people picking up the Easter eggs, oh, it's been a joy."

ScreenRant: "How much have you been paying attention to the theories online? Have you been following any conversations online that you're kind of, 'Oh, some of them are right, some of them are wrong!'"

Lauren Morais: "Definitely, who the Client is. I think that's so fun. There's been so many different theories and theories that I didn't see coming. I've been really enjoying that. Yeah, who the mysterious Client is. I've had friends in my own life ask me, and I was like, "No, you have to watch."

#3367. New Apple TV 4K remote’s best feature requires a newer iPhone model

A new Apple TV 4K releases this Friday (pre-order here), with an upgraded Siri Remote. But the new remote’s best feature might not work on your iPhone.

If you’re interested in the new Apple TV 4K launching this week, or perhaps you just want to buy the upgraded Siri Remote separately (available here), there’s a key limitation you should know.

Precision Finding on the new Siri Remote requires an iPhone 17 or newer.

The most common problem with the current Siri Remote is that it’s easy to lose. And once you lose it, Apple doesn’t offer many options for finding it. But that’s changing with the 4th gen Siri Remote.

You can use the new Siri Remote with any previous Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD model. And if you do, you’ll benefit from the remote’s new built-in speaker that can be triggered from the Find My app.

Joining the new speaker, the other main change with this latest Siri Remote is Precision Finding. If you’ve ever used the Find My app to track down a lost AirTag, you’ll probably be familiar with the feature.

Precision Finding lets you get step-by-step, guided directions that take you directly to the lost Siri Remote. It’s a huge upgrade from the old tool for finding the remote—which mostly just told you that it’s in your house somewhere.

But Precision Finding relies on the Bluetooth 6 support found in iPhone 17 and 17 Pro models (not iPhone 17e), iPhone Air, iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro models.

So if you don’t have one of those iPhones, you’ll still benefit from the built-in speaker that lets you play a sound to find the lost remote, but Precision Finding won’t be available.

You can buy the new Siri Remote for $59 on Amazon.

Will this limitation impact your Siri Remote purchase decision? Let us know in the comments.

#3366. Forget 'Peaky Blinders,' Titus Welliver's 8-Episode Crime Thriller Is Perfect From Start to Finish

Jeffrey is a freelance features writer at Collider. He is an MPA-accredited entertainment journalist and a Tomatometer-approved critic based in the LA area. He graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelor of Science in Radio, TV, & Film and a Bachelor of Arts in Theater.

If you're in the mood for a deliciously fun drama and a fan of shows like Peaky Blinders, it's time to check out The Westies. Set in the early 1980s, the MGM+ series presents a fictionalized account of the real-life Irish crime syndicate that operated out of Hell’s Kitchen. A combination of slick storytelling with crime drama thrills, along with a terrific cast of compelling characters, makes this show a must-watch experience.

The Westies mixes fact and fiction, with the series' main characters drawn from members of the real crime syndicate. Although the Italian mafia outnumbers the Westies five-to-one, the construction of the Javits Center in the latter's territory stands to give them a lucrative payout. J.K. Simmons stars as Eamon Sweeney, inspired by real Westies mob boss, Mickey Spillane. One of Sweeney's top lieutenants is Jimmy Roarke (Tom Brittney), based on real-life mobster James Coonan, whose loyalty to both the gang and its leader appears to be reaching its limits in the first season.

What did it take to bring the infamous Westies to television? J.K. Simmons, Tom Brittney, Titus Welliver, and co-creator/showrunner Chris Brancato pull back the curtain on how The Westies recreated 1980s Hell's Kitchen while balancing real history with dramatic storytelling.

When The Westies begins, Sweeney is attempting to navigate the finer points of the Javits construction deal while maintaining an uneasy peace with the Gambino crime family, led by Paul Castellano (Ron Lea) and underboss John Gotti (Hamish Allan-Headly) — and the series nicely juxtaposes these real-life figures against the story's more fictionalized interpretations. Although The Westies isn't aiming for a straightforward history lesson, with some elements of the show changed for storytelling purposes, series co-creators Chris Brancato and Michael Panes have crafted an immersive crime drama that exceptionally transports the audience back to the early 1980s.

Alongside the crime thriller's many twists and turns, The Westies boasts an incredible ensemble cast. The show has to juggle characters, factions, and subplots, but each still receives proper room to breathe. The actors wonderfully bring their characters to life, inhabiting a brutal world where one wrong move can bring ruin, and you are never sure who to trust. In addition to the intriguing chess game between Sweeney and Jimmy, another riveting subplot follows Jimmy's girlfriend, Bridget Walsh (Sarah Bolger), a former IRA soldier who now resides in the U.S. and runs into trouble when her former IRA contact and lover, Brendan Cahill (Allen Leech), arrives in New York City, seeking assistance with the IRA's ongoing activities.

Titus Welliver of Bosch fame is another standout within the cast as Glenn Keenan, a morally ambiguous NYPD officer who has a long-standing relationship with Sweeney. When FBI agent Birdie Polk (Jessica Frances Duke) recruits him to join her task force with the intention of bringing down organized crime, Keenan is torn between his ties to Sweeney and his love for his son, who is becoming involved with the Westies. Instead of choosing one, Keenan plays both sides of the law, and the actor portrays his character’s moral complexity exceptionally well. It's a different side of his acting strengths, and fans can watch him play someone totally different from his arguably most iconic role as Detective Harry Bosch.

The Westies hasn't yet been renewed for a second season, so its future is still up in the air. The first season ended on a shocking note with huge story implications, and it would be a shame if the finale served as the end of the road for the series. Brancato spoke optimistically about the show's fate in a July interview with Deadline, stating, 'We're very confident there will be a second season of The Westies."

The titular gang's rise to power has only just begun, and based on the first season's ending, there are many more great storylines to come. Nevertheless, The Westies provides a throwback crime drama experience reminiscent of movies like Goodfellas and Casino, albeit in a nostalgic 1980s setting.

#3365. Everything You Should Know About Black Friday 2026 Sales: Early Deals, Dates, and Retailers

As is often the case with major sales these days, retailers are increasingly blurring the lines between early deals and the official start of a sale. Black Friday sales appear to be becoming a month-long event, with early deals appearing in the first week of the month. If you haven't been paying attention, major retailers have already put out their plans and even started churning out deals. But you're still in time to make this upcoming Black Friday sale a great one. Here is everything you need to know to prepare you for the big sale.

Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving. This year, Black Friday starts at midnight on Nov. 27. Cyber Monday is the Monday following Black Friday, which starts at midnight on Nov. 30.

The major retailers doing sales are the usual: Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Home Depot, and many others. Currently, Walmart has publicized its plans already and has early deals available. Best Buy is offering one of the largest Black Friday and Cyber Week sales, with multiple events and early deals. Target has a three-day event. Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

Unlike Spring or Summer sales, Black Friday doesn't focus on specific categories, which means everything is fair game for discounts. In previous years, we've seen tech, tools, fitness equipment, outdoor supplies and furniture, bedding, video games, kitchen appliances, and more. This is one of the best times to make a list of what you need. You're likely to find what you're looking for discounted, and probably at its lowest price it has ever been. If you'd like to avoid having to do all that work, we always vet all of our deals for you. Just follow our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Prime Day and Black Friday are the two best times of the year to get the best deals on most purchases. Of course, depending on what you're shopping for, you might find other opportunities throughout the year, but in general, Prime Day and Black Friday have the best sales.

#3361. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

When you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

WebRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

But the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

If you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

While this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:

We’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

In case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

There’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

One of my favorite additions to Messages this year, Suggested Actions, debuts in iOS 27.2.

Suggested Actions appear underneath messages in a conversation when relevant. They can suggest creating a calendar event or reminder, adding to a note, and more based on the context of the message.

The feature was originally part of the iOS 27 beta this summer, but didn’t make the public build. Now it’s back in iOS 27.2, new and improved. There’s also an option to fine-tune which types of suggestions you’ll see.

Read more: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite

Every major streaming service has its own profiles feature, letting users on the same account keep their viewing history and recommendations separate. Apple TV has long offered such a feature in tvOS, but now with iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 it’s coming to iPhone and iPad too.

When you launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll be greeted by a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it if you don’t want to see if again. But if you ever share your iPhone with kids, the new profiles feature should come in handy.

Read more: iOS 27.2 gives Apple TV a new profiles feature on iPhone

Dual Capture is one of FaceTime’s best new features in years. Added in iOS 27, on compatible iPhones it lets you keep your front and rear cameras both active at the same time while on a FaceTime call.

iOS 27.2 brings a key upgrade to Dual Capture: it’s now available for Group FaceTime calls.

To use the feature, just hit the flip camera button like usual, and by default on iPhone 17 and newer you’ll stream both camera feeds simultaneously.

Read more: iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime’s best new feature even better

Timed with its new Home products push, Apple adds a pair of new Home app features in iOS 27.2 for compatible smart locks.

‘Lock After Closing’ is a new automation setting that lets you choose how long after a door is closed that it should lock automatically. Previously you could only set a duration based on the time since a door was unlocked, not closed.

‘Door Left Open’ tackles a related, but distinct problem: a door being left open too long. With compatible locks, you can configure the Home app to automatically notify you if a door has been left open for a certain period of time.

Read more: iOS 27.2 has three new changes just added this week

Apple Podcasts keeps getting better, with AI-powered automatic chapters and transcripts some of my favorite features. And in iOS 27.2, Apple has a welcome change to the Up Next queue on the Home tab.

Up Next is now split into two separate queues: New Episodes and Continue Playing.

Without the redesigned Health app, none of the new features appeal to me all that much. But performance improvements, bug fixes, and security fixes are always welcomed. What most of really wants is faster and more reliable Siri AI, along with support for a wider range of personal data, such as PDF documents on the iCloud Drive.

New Episodes contains only the latest episodes from shows you follow, while Continue Playing is a hub for all the episodes you’ve previously started but haven’t yet finished.

Apple’s Games app introduces some small updates in iOS 27.2 as well.

The Home tab now shows you recently downloaded games that you haven’t yet played. Previously, you would only see games with some play activity. And Apple says achievement progress and leaderboard scores have been updated in the Home tab to be easier to track. Finally, the Friends tab “provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages” per Apple.

Which new iOS 27.2 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

#3359. Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' a Box Office Hit, Fan-Favorite Years After Court Drama

Johnny Depp's return to the big screen landed at No. 1 at the international and domestic box offices this weekend years after his court drama ... despite a wide divide between critics and regular moviegoers.

"Ebenezer" opened domestically to the tune of $19 million and earned an additional $23 million overseas ... according to Variety and Deadline. Not bad for a budget of $38 million!

While the movie has split critics down the middle -- with the film sporting a 54% Tomatometer -- audiences have raved over it.

Currently the comeback flick is verified hot on Rotten Tomatoes with an 89% Popcornmeter rating ... and an A- CinemaScore.

The divide between fan reaction and critical response comes amid a flurry of analytical pieces that have tied the movie to some sort of PR power play by Johnny.

Take the Wall Street Journal's feature that says the film is the perfect PR vehicle for the star, while in a separate review, the WSJ claims the film fails to find its tone and that Johnny is "ridiculously blustery and loud as Ebenezer, as if trying to get laughs."

In another review ... Vanity Fair drew parallels further between Ebenezer and Johnny, characterizing the movie as "Christmas-washing" his reputation.

Johnny's return to Hollywood comes after he levied a defamation lawsuit against ex-wife Amber Heard over her 2018 Washington Post op-ed, in which she described herself as a "public figure representing domestic abuse." He claimed the piece falsely implied he was the abuser.

While a jury awarded Johnny millions in damages after siding with him, Heard won one count in her countersuit.

All in all ... it seems that Scrooges aside, Johnny has done it all in one weekend, returning to screens all over the world in a triumphant way.

#3358. Game Of Thrones Officially Brings Back Tywin Lannister In The Lion's Reign

Game of Thrones might have jumped the shark somewhat during its final season, but there's still plenty of love for the fantasy franchise, if you are able to quash those memories and leave them in the past. The best evidence for that is just how many other adaptations there are out there right now, giving fans plenty of options, regardless of what medium they tend to inhabit.

Game of Thrones: War for Westeros is a great example, launching in 2027 and giving players the chance to lead any of the show's major factions in their ultimate quest for the Iron Throne. There are also ongoing adaptations that continue to release regular updates, including one which is about to thrust one of the book's most calculated characters back to the fore.

Game of Thrones is full of all kinds of scheming characters, from those who are loyal to nobody, like Littlefinger, to those who are simply trying to make it through life in as good a shape as possible (a la Tyrion). Arguably the figure who is most successful in their machinations, though, is the Lannister patriarch Tywin, who leads arguably the most powerful family in Westeros at the time of the books.

He's about to serve as a central figure in the latest set of events for Game of Thrones: Legends, the mobile puzzle role-playing game by Zynga that is available for both iOS and Android. The game essentially tasks players with color-matching gems in order to defeat opponents.

The latest event is Kingsroad: The Lion’s Reign, which is set to run from November 9, at 3:00 a.m. ET to December 7, at 2:00 a.m. ET. Set around the very important Kingsroad and Goldroad, there are a bunch of Daily and Weekly Quests to complete for rewards that you would otherwise struggle to accrue in the usual gameplay loop.

In breaking down both the events, the developer shared the following insight:

"Kingsroad: Complete Daily and Weekly Goals to earn Kingsroad points, and progress along the Kingsroad for rewards! Earn 300 points on each of your five Daily Goals, and 800 points for each Weekly goal to reach new Tiers every day. This season’s Kingsroad rewards include Common Champion Shards for the Lannister Spearman, Summoning Tokens, and more! Beyond Tier 50, you can claim a bonus chest of rewards for every 700 points!

"Goldroad: This season’s Goldroad rewards include 15 Legendary Champion Shards for Tywin Lannister (The Hand). Upgrade to Elite Goldroad Pass to earn Exalted Tokens, Legendary Gear, Splendid, Grand, and Forge Summon Tokens, Valyrian Essence, Skill Books, and other bonuses on top of the Kingsroad rewards. Progress through the Tiers to earn more rewards for unlocking and powering up Champions!"

It's worth noting that the Elite Goldroad Pass will cost real world money, though it absolutely isn't necessary to play the game in its current state.

Outside of that, fans of George RR Martin's universe can look forward to the final season of House of the Dragon in 2028, as well as the second season of the excellent Knight of the Seven Kingdoms next year. Don't count on that Game of Thrones Season 8 reshoot any time soon though.

#3357. Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

There’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

According to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

The easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

#3355. 25 Years Ago, The Lord of the Rings Became a Horror Movie for One Perfect Scene

Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

The skeleton is already down the well when the chain starts to go, and the worst part is realizing how much of it is still up there. In The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, Pippin (Billy Boyd) has plenty of time to stand there and think about what he’s done. So does everybody watching. A skeleton falling down a well is a pretty good gag on its own. Let the chain drag the noise out long enough, and suddenly you’re wondering how far sound travels through a mountain.

It helps that Peter Jackson has spent the movie making the Hobbits’ screwups funny. Pippin asking about second breakfast is part of what makes him good company, and a wizard telling him off for touching something he shouldn’t feels like a scene you already know how to watch. There’s even a little relief when Gandalf (Ian McKellen) starts yelling. If he has time to call Pippin an idiot, maybe getting yelled at is the worst thing that’s about to happen to him. Then the drums start in Balin’s tomb, and the Fellowship gets to hear a sound that, until a few seconds ago, belonged to the dead. That’s the moment The Fellowship of the Ring becomes a horror movie. Gandalf has just read what happened to the last people who tried to hold this room, and the drums are the first indication that the Fellowship could die the exact same way. Suddenly, knowing the history of Moria makes being there worse.

Gimli (John Rhys-Davies) is the reason the tomb feels like a loss before it feels like a trap. He’s been talking about the welcome his cousin will give them, which is the kind of promise that gets you through a miserable trip. The shaft of daylight in that chamber makes it look like they’ve finally found somewhere they can stop. It falls right on Balin’s grave. There’s something especially cruel about giving Gimli enough light to see exactly what he came all that way to find.

The book does something nastier with that same sense of recognition. The Dwarves who held the chamber were thinking about the same things the Fellowship has to think about now. Which halls are still safe? How long will the door hold? Where can everybody go if it gives? “We cannot get out” lands so harshly because the Watcher in the Water has already brought down the entrance behind them. Gandalf is reading somebody else’s last words in a room where they could just as easily belong to him.

That’s also why the scene can get so much out of a drumbeat. A growl would tell the Fellowship there’s something down there. Drums tell them there are enough of whatever’s down there to organize. By the time Boromir (Sean Bean) announces that they have a cave troll, the joke buys about a second of relief. He’s just looked through the door the Dwarves once had to defend, and his best idea is to shut it again.

Jackson spends the fight at the tomb teaching the audience how hard it is to keep the Orcs out of a room. When they surround the Fellowship in the pillared hall, they’ve finally got what they wanted. Then a roar carries through the stone, the hall starts to glow, and the Orcs give up a fight they’re about to win. After watching them bring a cave troll to a nine-person fight, there’s something deeply upsetting about finding out what they consider a bad idea.

Gandalf’s reaction makes it worse. In the dark earlier, he could sit down with Frodo (Elijah Wood) and make the whole problem of being lost in Moria feel manageable. When he tells Aragorn (Viggo Mortensen) that swords are useless here, it takes away the one thing the Fellowship could still count on after the tomb. They knew how to fight their way through a room, but now the person who knows the most about what’s coming is telling them to run. The bridge gives Gandalf a chance to do the thing a fantasy hero is supposed to do. He stands his ground, breaks the stone beneath the Balrog, and sends it down into the dark. It’s a win for just long enough that the audience can start thinking about getting out of Moria again. Then the whip comes back up. The same darkness that hid the Balrog on its way in hides the last thing it does to Gandalf, right up until it catches him by the ankle.

The series hails from ‘Star Trek: Picard’ and ‘VisionQuest’ showrunner Terry Matalas.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power gets to make the Balrog scary from the other side of that history. When King Durin III (Peter Mullan) breaks into the mithril cavern in the Season 2 finale, there’s a whole city above him that the audience has actually spent time in. The horror of the scene is how quickly Durin understands what he’s put at risk. His son gets his father back in the moment Durin takes off the ring, and there’s barely time to register that before he charges the creature.

With Season 3 on Prime Video and Simon Pegg voicing the Balrog, the creature gets to tell us something about itself. 25 years earlier, however, Jackson had a nastier idea: he let the last Dwarf in Balin’s tomb tell us what it sounded like to die down there, then made the Fellowship listen for the same sound.
